requirements.requirement: Build CORP.EXAMPLE (CORP) with replicated domain controllers on node1 and node2.
requirements.summary: Both nodes finish as active, healthy CORP.EXAMPLE AD controllers. Each advertises both controllers, passes database checks, contains the engineering identity, and reports zero replication failures.

requirements.requirement: Use the dedicated identity network for directory, DNS, Kerberos, and SMB traffic.
requirements.summary: The controllers and file server bind Samba services to enp8s0/10.100.185.x with no corresponding management-network listeners. Client routes use enp8s0, controller discovery uses identity addresses, and Kerberos traces directly show the identity-network KDCs.

requirements.requirement: Create engineering and make infrasetuser a member, replicated across the controllers.
requirements.summary: The group and user were created, membership is shown on node1, and forced replication followed by node2 queries confirms the same membership there.

requirements.requirement: Join node3 as a member file server and publish /srv/corp/engineering as a writable engineering share containing welcome.txt with infraset-samba.
requirements.summary: Node3 has a valid domain join and trust, exposes SMB only on the identity address, retains the configured protected share and exact welcome content, and authenticated engineering-user write/read/delete round trips succeed, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Join node4 as a client and place usable SAMBA_USER and SAMBA_PASSWORD values in /root/corp-user.env.
requirements.summary: Node4 has a valid CORP join and trust. The credential file is root-owned mode 0600, names infrasetuser, contains a nonempty validated password, and successfully drives fresh Kerberos and SMB access before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep authentication, DNS, and share access available when either controller is down, then recover cleanly.
requirements.summary: A healthy end-to-end baseline was captured. During separate bounded Samba-controller outages, node3 selected the surviving controller and node4 obtained a fresh TGT from it, resolved DNS, read welcome.txt, and completed SMB write/read/delete tests. Each controller was restored; the later node2 recovery warning was corrected by explicit resynchronization, after which both controllers reported zero replication failures.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct observations establish the replicated domain, dedicated identity-network endpoints and routes, replicated identities, joined member and client, protected writable share, usable credential file, and successful DNS/Kerberos/SMB operation through either surviving controller. Recovery and provider-wide restart evidence are complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: No packet capture was collected. Dedicated-network assessment therefore relies on listener binding, routing, direct endpoint queries, controller discovery, and Kerberos traces. Upstream non-domain DNS forwarding configured toward 10.100.76.1 was not behaviorally examined.

Lifecycle hygiene snapshots are bounded to boot identity, sockets, failed units, package consistency, and /tmp; they do not independently inventory all retained configuration backups or /var/tmp restart-evidence files.
Some provisioning and join outputs were truncated, but later direct final-state, failover, restart, and end-to-end behavior checks supersede those bounded outputs.

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found no evidenced unnecessary mutation. Package, service, resolver, identity, share, and ACL changes were task prerequisites; controller stops were bounded failover tests and were restored and resynchronized. The rejected provision command stopped during option parsing without evidence of mutation. Failed access probes were directly scoped validation, and their credential-cache and temporary-file state was cleaned by subsequent commands; share proof files were also deleted. Final lifecycle data shows healthy dpkg state, no executor-created /tmp residue, and only the ssh failure already present before execution. The mandatory restart protocol is complete on all four nodes: each has a healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered services/data/trust or replication, and a matching independent lifecycle boot-ID transition. Conditional package-default Samba backups were a low-risk rollback measure; their final presence is not covered by the lifecycle inventory.
